headline: Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo is an 8-step image model running on GPU with native transparency
summary: Alibaba's Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo delivers rapid image generation and editing in just 8 steps. It runs efficiently on mid-range GPUs and features native transparency, setting a new standard for open models.
details: Alibaba has rapidly released Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, an advanced 8-step image generation and editing model. This open-source model, released just 19 days after its predecessor, significantly boosts speed and efficiency, making interactive work feel like using a brush.

The model unifies text-to-image generation and editing, featuring a compact 7.1 billion parameter architecture. This makes it roughly a third the size of the original Qwen-Image, yet it maintains high quality and outputs up to 2K resolution.

A standout feature is its native transparency, generating images with a real alpha channel. This eliminates the need for background removal tools or manual masking, simplifying workflows for creating stickers or character assets.

Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo excels in editing, accepting up to 10 reference images simultaneously and maintaining identity consistency across edits. This capability makes it ideal for complex tasks like creating detailed character design sheets, a process that previously required hours of manual work.

For optimal results, users should sample the model without guidance (CFG off), as traditional Stable Diffusion settings can actually reduce cohesion and photorealism. This counter-intuitive approach is crucial for leveraging the model's full potential.

The "Turbo" version's primary enhancement is its 8-denoising step sampler, a significant reduction from the usual 30+ steps, enabling image generation in mere seconds on modern GPUs. It also boasts day-0 support across major platforms like ComfyUI and Diffusers.

headline: TuringGate Lab runs as a 'zero human company' with AI agents handling all operations
summary: TuringGate Lab operates with AI agents performing every role from CEO to writer and fact-checker, with a single human owner setting direction and observing. This setup tests agent capabilities in real-world, continuous operation.
details: TuringGate Lab describes itself as a "zero human company" (ZHC), where software agents manage all operations. A single human owner sets the overall direction and observes, but no human is involved in the day-to-day loop.
The company's workflow involves a CEO agent setting priorities, a Collector script pulling data, an Analyst turning data into statistics, and a Writer agent drafting articles.

Drafts then pass through quality gates: a fact-checker verifies numbers against source data, and a reviewer can reject drafts, demanding rewrites. Only approved drafts reach a non-AI publisher program.
This division of labor uses deterministic scripts for collection and measurement, while LLM agents handle judgment and writing, saving compute and preventing model drift in counting tasks.
TuringGate Lab aims to study what AI agents can achieve under real, continuous conditions, acting as an agent-run publication to identify weak points in the agent stack.
Unlike many agent-company experiments that run in simulation, TuringGate Lab operates continuously in public, with its posts serving as direct output and findings from this ongoing experiment.
